ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c. 17) and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2017, c. 21), as well as domestic PEP definitions under the PCMLTFA. Enhanced due diligence and written risk assessment are required for any domestic or foreign politically exposed persons. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years in accordance with FINTRAC record-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ServiceOntario – Ontario Business and Limited Partnership Name Search
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in English or French using the 26 Latin letters; accents and diacritical marks are permitted; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into English or French. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered business name, limited partnership, or trademark, and phonetic equivalents are assessed during the NUANS search review.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may request reconsideration from the Ontario Director under the Business Names Act within 30 days, providing written reasons and supporting evidence. If the Director denies the appeal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Ontario Superior Court of Justice. Alternatively, the applicant may re-file using a revised name with a letter of consent from the affected party or a slight modification that avoids confusing similarity. All NUANS search reports and correspondence must be preserved as part of the due diligence record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for mail forwarding and process service, but the limited partnership must maintain a physical office address in Ontario as its principal place of business. A post office box is prohibited. A virtual-office provider is acceptable if the contract includes physical document storage, service-of-process capability, and a registered agent address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; projected at less than 5% per annum for a digital webtoon publishing limited partnership classified as FINTRAC Low_Risk_Standard. The Canada Revenue Agency may conduct a site visit to verify business number records, and FINTRAC may perform an AML/CFT examination requiring document production, but an unannounced physical premises search is not anticipated for this low-risk industry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, ss. 2-7 (formation), s. 8 (registration), s. 10 (false filings); Business Names Registration Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.13 (name registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Partnerships Division
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory paid-up capital for a limited partnership; contributions may be cash, property, or services as agreed in the partnership agreement. No escrow account requirement under Ontario law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the corporate general partner accepts the limited partners' subscription commitments and records contributed capital as set forth in the partnership register. That the registered office of the limited partnership be established at [Registered Office Address], Ontario, and the designated Registered Office Representative be appointed to accept process. That [Name] be appointed Chief Compliance Officer and [Name] be appointed Managing General Partner, with full authority to execute filings, open bank accounts, and engage tax advisers. That the Secretary certify these resolutions and file the necessary declaration promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct Name Search and Prepare General Partner Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery via Ontario Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a restricted name search for the proposed limited partnership name to confirm availability and distinguishability. Confirm that the corporate general partner is in good standing and that its board has authorized the creation of the limited partnership. Prepare and notarize the partnership agreement, including capital contribution schedules and authority provisions.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership certificate name
Corporate general partner articles of incorporation and certificate of status
Draft Limited Partnership Agreement with contribution schedule
Name search report issued by authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search discloses a conflict, file a new name or obtain the conflicting party's written consent plus an affidavit of non-use, then resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Companies and Partnerships Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 Declaration in both English and French or English only as appropriate. Include the general partner's name, registered office address, and the authorized signing officer. Submit electronically through the Ontario Business Registry and pay the statutory filing fee by credit card.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Declaration of Limited Partnership
Name search report
Written authorization from the corporate general partner to file
Registered office street address and municipal description
Proof of general partner identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry issues a Notice of Query or rejects the declaration, correct the stated defects and resubmit within 30 days. If the registration lapses, pay the late renewal or reinstatement fee and file a fresh declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Registered Office and Registered Representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the registered office is a physical address in Ontario and not solely a post-office box. Confirm the appointment of a registered representative to accept service of process. File any change using Form 2 if the office or representative changes after initial registration.
required_dossiers: Form 2 if a change is required
Proof of registered office address consent from landlord or occupier
Written consent of the registered representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to maintain a registered office may lead to administrative dissolution; file a late change and pay the prescribed penalty to restore compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Federal Business Number and Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Ontario declaration certificate to register the limited partnership for a federal Business Number. Open a GST/HST account if annual taxable supply exceeds 30,000 CAD, and register for payroll, import/export, or other accounts only when triggered by actual operations.
required_dossiers: Ontario declaration registration certificate
Limited partnership agreement and general partner resolution
Canadian business bank account details
General partner legal entity documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, respond with corrected entity information through Business Registration Online and request a retroactive effective date where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Establish Payment Rail Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered Canadian bank under the federal Bank Act and commercial payment processors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the declaration certificate and partnership agreement to open a Canadian dollar operating account. Designate the banking officer and provide authorized signatory forms. If the webtoon platform uses app stores, complete merchant onboarding with Apple IAP and Google Play Billing using the LP's legal registration documents.
required_dossiers: Form 1 declaration certificate
Limited partnership agreement
Corporate general partner board resolution authorizing bank account
Government-issued identification of all principals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor questions signatory authority, provide a certified incumbency certificate from the corporate general partner and resubmit the account application.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via My Business Account portal; Ontario Ministry of Finance and Ontario Business Registry for provincial registration and extra-provincial limited partnership licensing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership obtains a federal Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 with the CRA online or by mail. For Ontario, the limited partnership must register as an extra-provincial limited partnership under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act through the Ontario Business Registry. The CRA BN is the primary tax identification number, and a separate GST/HST account is created with the BN plus a two-letter program indicator. Non-resident partners without Canadian social insurance numbers may use an individual tax number or partnership BN for reporting. Ontario uses the federal BN for provincial tax administration and does not issue a separate corporate identity number to a limited partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Canadian income tax treats a limited partnership as fiscally transparent and not a separate taxpayer; income, losses, and credits are allocated to partners under the partnership agreement and subject to the rules in the Income Tax Act for Canadian and non-resident partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election. A limited partnership cannot elect entity-level taxation for income tax purposes. The partners may, however, make a partnership designation under the Income Tax Act respecting fiscal period and allocation, and are required to file Schedule 50 under the T5013 partnership information return. Under the Excise Tax Act, a partnership and its members may jointly elect under section 273 to designate one member as the representative member responsible for filing and remitting GST/HST on behalf of the partnership. Certain hybrid mismatch and treaty elections may be available for cross-border partners under the Income Tax Act and Canada's tax treaties, subject to OECD BEPS implementation by way of anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax), a VAT-style federal consumption tax administered by the CRA, combined with the Ontario provincial HST component on taxable supplies made in Ontario.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies from Canadian activities in any single calendar quarter or the preceding four quarters for a person carrying on business in Canada; non-residents carrying on business in Canada that exceed the small-supplier threshold are required to register for GST/HST. A non-resident that solicits orders in Canada or is specifically required by the CRA may be required to register regardless of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada currently has no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing clearance regime for GST/HST. Electronic invoices are accepted provided they are legible and contain prescribed information under the Excise Tax Act. The Government of Canada is promoting the pan-Canadian e-invoicing standard (Peppol), but compliance remains voluntary. Ontario has no provincial electronic clearance requirement for HST.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating under Canadian GST/HST applies to supplies of tangible personal property that are exported and delivered by the supplier to an address outside Canada, and to supplies of services or intangible personal property made to a non-resident person where the supply is not for consumption, use, or enjoyment in Canada. Digital webtoon subscriptions and chapter unlocking sales should be zero-rated when delivered electronically to a non-resident subscriber and the recipient does not use the digital content in Canada. Supporting business-model evidence includes subscriber billing addresses, IP geolocation, app store/Google Play payment records, and digital delivery logs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or Canada Border Services Agency export documentation where physical goods are exported
Bill of Lading or air waybill for physical shipments
Commercial invoice and purchase order showing non-resident recipient and delivery outside Canada
Payment settlement records and inward remittance evidence from the app store or payment processor
Digital delivery logs and IP-based proof of foreign consumption for electronic webtoon supplies
T5013 partnership information return records and GST/HST zero-rated supply schedules
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess GST/HST returns to disallow zero-rating where the supplier fails to maintain contemporaneous documentary evidence of export or foreign consumption. Such reassessments carry statutory interest and may be subject to penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including a 10% gross negligence penalty on willful or grossly negligent false statements. In severe cases involving fraudulent export zero-rating, the CRA may impose additional penalties based on tax evaded and pursue criminal prosecution; output tax previously zero-rated is clawed back with retrospective effect and no offsetting input tax credits are allowed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and currency authority; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises federally chartered deposit-taking institutions; FINTRAC enforces cross-border EFT and virtual-currency reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada has no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration because no exchange-control regime exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a freely floating and fully convertible currency. Both current-account flows (subscription revenue, chapter-unlocking royalties, licensing fees) and capital-account flows (LP capital contributions, profit distributions, loan repayments) are unrestricted and require no prior regulatory approval. Remittance frictions are procedural: (i) Statistics Canada Balance of Payments reporting for material non-resident direct investment; (ii) FINTRAC reporting for international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more; (iii) platform settlement timing from Apple/Google treasury entities; (iv) Part XIII withholding on separate payments of royalties, interest, or management fees to non-residents (25% statutory, generally 15% under the Canada-US Treaty), while a non-resident LP partner's allocated share of Canadian-source business income is reported via T5013 and taxed on a net basis under Part I. No profit-remittance approval or FX allocation rights apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion ratio. Digital-content export receipts (webtoon subscription, chapter-unlocking, and in-app purchase revenue from non-residents) may be held indefinitely in CAD, USD, EUR, or other currencies in Canada or offshore. Only Income Tax Act section 261 functional-currency rules and internal treasury policy govern the currency mix.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium - supplementary disbursement rail only. FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (Wise Canada, Airwallex, Payoneer) provide low-cost multicurrency creator payouts and virtual IBANs, but under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) payment service providers must register with the Bank of Canada, and foreign EMI licences (UK FCA, EU EMD/MiCA) do not pass-port into Canada. Primary platform settlement (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing net proceeds) must be held at a CDIC-member Schedule I bank; MSB accounts should be limited to batched micropayments under a documented counterparty-risk policy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted for an Ontario-registered limited partnership. Schedule I banks require: (i) a live video interview with the General Partner's authorized signatories and directors; (ii) notarized or corporately certified Ontario limited partnership registration, LP agreement, and General Partner resolutions; (iii) proof of registered office and Ontario operating address; and (iv) at least one authorized signatory with a verifiable Canadian nexus. If the General Partner is itself foreign or any UBO is a non-resident individual, the bank may mandate an in-person attestation at a Canadian branch or an apostilled KYC package. US partners must provide W-8IMY or W-8BEN-E depending on the LP's flow-through classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-tier ownership with concentrated non-resident US partners and discretionary trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario limited partnership registration record; full UBO organigram with percentage interests; General Partner resolution authorizing account opening; trust deed or declaration where applicable; source-of-wealth narrative and bank references for each 25%+ UBO; confirmation of no bearer shares or nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared comic/webtoon syndication activity and expected high-volume, low-ticket settlement flows from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play distribution agreement; monthly settlement mechanics and projected volume curves by market; sample historical or pro forma settlement statements; NAICS 511130 / ISIC 9000 classification letter from a licensed Canadian accountant; app store listing evidence and content moderation policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border creator payouts to jurisdictions with elevated money-laundering typologies (KR, ID, PH, BR) for licensing royalties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Creator/rightsholder registry with individual KYC files; executed licensing and exclusivity agreements; series and chapter metadata ownership trail; scheduled payout register with FX calculations; OFAC/OSFI/EU sanctions screening certificates; confirmation that no crypto-denominated settlement is used; annual independent AML review for the payout program.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections from non-resident LP partners lacking documented partnership commitment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Amended limited partnership agreement with capital account schedule; board-approved capital call notices matching each wire; partner bank statements (redacted) showing source of funds; Statistics Canada Balance of Payments filing acknowledgment; tax opinion confirming passive pass-through eligibility; updated Ontario LP registration if partner composition changes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-content platform revenue creating perceived virtual-asset or gambling-adjacent exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written anti-crypto corporate treasury policy confirming fiat-only settlement from Apple/Google; age-gating and geo-content compliance statement; transaction-monitoring participation consent; complete sub-ledger transparency for all platform settlement files; absence of any gaming, sweepstakes, or NFT mechanics in the webtoon product.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident LP partners contribute equity via SWIFT MT103/202 to the LP's CAD operating account at the Ontario Schedule I bank. Remittance Information field 70 must include 'CA-LP Capital Contribution - [Partner Name] - [Date]' and the Ontario LP registration number, and each wire must match a board-approved capital call. USD wires clear through the bank's US correspondent (e.g., JPMorgan Chase for RBC, BMO Harris for BMO, Citibank for CIBC) and convert to CAD at spot or a pre-booked forward. International EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more require FINTRAC reporting; direct-investment transactions meeting Statistics Canada thresholds require Balance of Payments filing. No Investment Canada Act review applies to a greenfield LP funding without acquisition of an existing Canadian business. Any new partner admission requires concurrent amendment of the Ontario LP registration and updated CRS/FATCA self-certification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Creator royalties and licensing fees are contractually settled on open-account terms (2-4 business days) and cleared as follows: (i) SWIFT MT103 for creator bank accounts in KR, US, EU, JP, ID, PH, and BR - SEPA via IBAN, Fedwire/ABA for the US, KFTC for Korea; (ii) batched micropayments below USD 5,000 routed through a FINTRAC-registered MSB (Wise or equivalent) at capped monthly volume to control remittance costs; (iii) commercial letters of credit are not applicable to webtoon micro-royalties and are expressly excluded from the treasury policy. Inbound platform revenue is received as net monthly settlements: Apple distribution via Apple Canada Inc. / Apple Distribution International (CAD/USD) and Google Play via Google LLC / Google Ireland Limited (USD/CAD), swept into the operational account and reconciled automatically against the settlement sub-ledger. USD-denominated creator payouts are funded directly from the USD account to avoid double conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD vanilla forwards (tenors up to 12 months) booked with a Schedule I bank treasury desk under the bank's Master Forward or ISDA 2002/CSA documentation
FX swaps and swap-point rollovers to align settlement-date mismatches among Apple/Google payout timing, monthly creator runs, and operating-expense cycles
Zero-cost collars (vanilla long-call/short-put structures) on CAD/USD to cap conversion cost while retaining upside on surplus CAD
Deliverable CAD/EUR and CAD/JPY forwards for European and Japanese creator and platform payables
Cross-currency swap (CAD/USD fixed/floating or floating/floating) strictly for asset-liability management if the LP later issues debt or enters a term treasury facility

Offshore USD/KRW non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing USD/KRW to hedge Korean creator-royalty liabilities, layered with a CAD/USD forward (KRW is not fully convertible offshore; no deliverable CAD/KRW NDF exists)
Hedge-only mandate: no speculative or naked positions permitted; all dealer counterparties limited to OSFI-regulated Canadian Schedule I banks and their OECD-regulated affiliates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Limited Partnership Annual Return (business information confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Government of Ontario, Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within six months after the limited partnership's fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year LP, on or before June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee of CAD 100 (approx. USD 73) on the first overdue day; if the Annual Return remains unfiled for more than two consecutive fiscal periods, the Registrar serves notice and may administratively cancel (strike off) the LP's registration; reinstatement requires the up-to-date Annual Return, all outstanding Declarations of Change, and payment of reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaration of Change / Amended Declaration under the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act (partner changes, capital contributions, registered office, business activity updates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Government of Ontario, Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after the date of any change in the registered particulars; annual re-verification is performed during the Annual Return cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each overdue Declaration is subject to a CAD 100 (approx. USD 73) late charge; materially stale particulars expose the LP to Registry rectification measures and, on 60 days' notice, administrative cancellation of the LP registration, leaving the General Partner with unrestricted personal liability for partnership obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013 SUMMARY and T5013 slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following a December 31 fiscal period; where any limited partner is a corporation, no later than six months after the fiscal period end (June 30 for a calendar-year LP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 20 per day to a maximum of CAD 2,500 (minimum CAD 100); each late T5013 slip adds CAD 25 per day up to 100 slips; the CRA may also disallow flow-through losses allocated to partners until the return is filed and may reassess prior taxation years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST Return (GST34) under the Excise Tax Act — annual filer election
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the LP's fiscal year, coinciding with the T5013 preparation cycle for webtoon platform revenues
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 4% of the balance outstanding plus 1% per month of compounding arrears (Excise Tax Act, section 280), with daily prescribed interest; confirmed non-filing cancels the annual-filer election and may trigger instalment demands.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit is imposed on a private Ontario limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Act, RSO 1990, c. L.8. A statutory or contractual audit becomes mandatory only when: (i) the LP agreement, subscription agreement or syndication deed requires audited statements; (ii) the LP engages in a prospectus-exempt offering of limited partnership units under OSC Rule 45-106 requiring audited financial statements; (iii) the managing general partner receives a written demand from limited partners holding at least 25% of the profit interests and the partnership agreement contains an audit-upon-demand clause; or (iv) CRA makes a formal written demand under the Income Tax Act for audited support of the T5013 return. The webtoon-syndication LP described in this dossier does not meet any of these thresholds and is expected to arrange an independent review engagement instead.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook, Accounting, Part II) applies as the local GAAP for a private Ontario LP; IFRS (Part I) applies only if the LP elects IFRS or becomes publicly accountable. Multi-language chapter-unlock revenue is recognized under ASPE Section 3400 or IFRS 15, and Apple IAP / Google Play Billing commissions are reported net of platform settlement where the LP is acting as agent for the platform.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario does not maintain a separate public UBO register for limited partnerships. Under the Limited Partnerships Act, the LP's registered declaration must at all times reflect the general and limited partners, and any transfer, redemption or admission of a limited partner must be filed as a Declaration of Change within 15 days. Each annual cycle, the General Partner conducts an ownership reconciliation at fiscal year-end, obtains certified ultimate-individual ownership schedules from any corporate limited partner, records the confirmation in the partnership minute book, and certifies the continuity of UBO data to the registered agent as the basis for the Annual Return and T5013 filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (name, address, capital contributed, withdrawals, and profit-share percentage)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (15% federal plus 11.5% Ontario) combined general corporate income tax rate; the Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent, and taxable income is assessable at the partner level at each partner's applicable marginal or corporate rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: combined 12.2% (9% federal plus 3.2% Ontario) on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income where the partner is a qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation; SR&ED refundable investment tax credits up to 35% for CCPCs and 15% non-refundable for other corporations; Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (10% refundable on qualifying Ontario labour expenditures for qualifying interactive digital content); accelerated capital cost allowance for computer software, copyright catalogues, and digital platforms.
